title: Votes for women
examples: When did women finally get the right to vote in many countries?
What is the difference between a suffragette and a suffragist?
Can you tell me about the early fights for women's voting rights?

explain.say: Today we learn about women fighting for the vote. We will look at the suffragists and suffragettes.
The suffragists believed in peaceful ways to gain the vote. They organized marches and wrote letters to leaders.
The suffragettes used more dramatic actions to get attention. They sometimes engaged in civil disobedience.
New Zealand was a very early place to grant this right. They gave women the vote in eighteen ninety three.
The fight for the vote happened all over the world. Many countries eventually granted women the right to vote.
In everyday life, this idea shows how groups can push for change. Think about a school rule that needs changing.

items: A group petitioning for better lunch options

faq.q: Why is there a difference between suffragettes and suffragists?
faq.a: Suffragists focused on peaceful methods like lobbying. Suffragettes used more confrontational tactics to gain attention.
asks: What is the difference between the two groups?

faq.q: Was New Zealand the very first place to give women the vote?
faq.a: New Zealand was one of the very early places to grant this right. The fight happened in many places at different times.
asks: When did the vote happen in New Zealand?

faq.q: What does 'civil disobedience' mean in this context?
faq.a: It means openly breaking a law you believe is unfair. This was a tactic used to force people to listen.
asks: Is breaking the law okay sometimes?

faq.q: Did the fight for the vote end quickly?
faq.a: No, it was a long and difficult struggle. It involved decades of organizing and protesting across many nations.

faq.q: What was the main goal of all these movements?
faq.a: The main goal was achieving suffrage, which means the right to vote in elections.

facts: Suffragists generally used peaceful methods like lobbying and writing.
Suffragettes sometimes used more direct and visible forms of protest.
New Zealand granted women the right to vote in eighteen ninety three.
The fight for voting rights was a global movement over many years.

quiz.say: The initial, peaceful efforts to gain voting rights were mainly carried out by the:
quiz.why: The suffragists were known for their organized, peaceful lobbying and petitioning efforts.

wrong.0: Politicians were the people who held the power to grant the vote, not the activists themselves.
wrong.1: The government was the institution that made the laws, not the group fighting for the change.
wrong.3: While they were part of the movement, the suffragettes are more associated with more direct action.

quiz.say: Which action best represents the more confrontational tactics used by some activists?
quiz.why: Civil disobedience involves breaking laws peacefully to protest injustice, which was a tactic used by some activists.

wrong.0: Writing letters is a peaceful, organized method, not a direct confrontation.
wrong.1: A tea party is a social event and does not represent a protest action.
wrong.2: Attending a meeting is participation, but not necessarily a direct challenge to the law.

quiz.say: If a country granted women the vote in eighteen ninety three, it was likely:
quiz.why: The lesson specifically mentioned New Zealand as an early example of this right being granted.

wrong.0: While England was involved, the specific early date points to New Zealand.
wrong.2: The US vote for women happened much later than the date mentioned.
wrong.3: The Roman Empire was a very different time period and context.
